articles.body:
DAZN announced Tuesday morning that Saved By The Bell and Extra alum Mario Lopez would be joining its Inside the Ring show.

What it didn't mention was that former host Max Kellerman and analyst LeSean McCoy wouldn't be there to greet him. According to Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , they will not be returning for the second season of the boxing show.

Boxing insider Mike Coppinger announced Monday that he would return to the program, noting it would now stream twice a week on DAZN Boxing and Ring Magazine's YouTube channels. That follows last week's report from Total Boxing that Saudi official Turki Alalshikh has agreed to sell a controlling interest in Ring Magazine to DAZN .

According to a write-up in Ring , Lopez will be the show's new full-time host, teaming with Coppinger and a rotating panel of analysts. The longtime actor is a major boxing enthusiast, serving as a guest color commentator for boxing events and co-hosting a boxing podcast, The 3 Knockdown Rule , with Ring contributor Steve Kim.

Per FOS, the change won't impact Kellerman's role calling matches for Zuffa Boxing , a joint venture between the Saudi Public Investment Fund and TKO.

It's been a tough week for the former ESPN talking head, who was slammed over comments he made about the recently announced Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight and accused of being a mouthpiece for Alalshikh's camp in their public feud with Dana White.

articles.title: Asian Games medals beyond the funding pipeline: Athletes who delivered despite modest support
articles.summary: New Delhi: India’s 21-gold campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has thrown up an interesting set of numbers: champions who reached the continental
articles.body: New Delhi: India’s 21-gold campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has thrown up an interesting set of numbers: champions who reached the continental podium despite receiving relatively modest targeted financial assistance under the govt’s elite-athlete programmes.Their stories do not diminish the broader support extended to Indian sport. Instead, they underline how performances can sometimes run ahead of the funding pipelines designed to identify and back medal prospects.The clearest example is 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod. A recently-inducted Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) athlete for the Aich-Nagoya preparatory cycle, Kumkum became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold at the Games, defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 after a shoot-off. She also won gold in the women’s recurve team event and silver in mixed team, ending the campaign with three medals and securing India an LA Olympics quota.The funding support extended to her puts her targeted assistance at just Rs 50,000. That is a striking figure against the scale of her achievement, even though her preparation also benefited from the budget allocated to the respective national sports federations (NSFs) under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC).The same pattern is visible in compound archery. Sahil Rajesh Jadhav, who helped India win mixed team gold with Chikitha Taniparthi and also contributed to the men’s team gold, received Rs 50,000 under TOPS during the Games cycle. His top podium finish also delivered India an Olympic quota in compound archery.Kushal Dalal and Thirumuru Ganesh Maniratnam, members of India’s men’s compound team that defeated China for gold, also received only Rs 50,000 each under TOPS during the cycle. Yet the trio of Dalal, Ganesh and Jadhav produced one of India’s five archery gold medals at the Games.The contrast becomes sharper when placed alongside athletes receiving substantially larger targeted allocations. Boxer Ankush Panghal, for instance, received Rs 75,000 under TOPS, while his other gold partners in boxing Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda received Rs 22.97 lakh and Rs 8.59 lakh assistance, respectively, during the Games cycle.These figures show that support was available at markedly different levels depending on an athlete’s classification, requirements, and timing within the system.Similarly, in sailing, Harshita Tomar and Shital Verma secured the bronze medal in the women’s skiff, with both athletes not being part of the TOPS programme. Also, in the same sport, sailors Manu Francis and Prince Noble won silver in the men’s skiff, but both were not part of either TOPS Core or Development group. Boxer Kapil Pokhariya, too, wasn't part of the TOPS.In shooting, the trio of Manisha Keer, Neeru Dhanda and Aashima Ahlawat won the silver medal in Trap women's team event, with Manisha receiving no TOPS assistance while Neeru, a TOPS Development athlete, getting Rs one lakh. In athletics, silver-wining javelin thrower Yashvir Singh wasn't part of the TOPS funding and largely prepared through the ACTC budget. In kurash, bronze-winner Pincky Balhara, competing in the -78 kg event, received Rs 75,000 under the TAGG scheme during the Games cycle.BOX:Low-targeted assistance medallists (under TOPS/TAGG):Archery: Kumkum Mohod (Rs 50,000), Sahil Jadhav (Rs 50,000), Kushal Dalal (Rs 50,000), Thirumuru Maniratnam (Rs 50,000), Boxing: Ankush (Rs 75,000), Kapil Pokhariya (not covered under TOPS); Shooting: Neeru Dhanda (Rs 1,00,000), Kurash: Pincky Balhara (Rs 75,000), Athletics: Seema (Rs 25,000), Baranica Elangoan and Yashvir Singh (both not covered under TOPS).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Congelación a la inclusión
articles.standfirst: El Gobierno ha ralentizado el impulso del deporte inclusivo no atendiendo la partida que reclaban las federaciones. Hay riesgo de desandar el camino
articles.summary: El Gobierno ha ralentizado el impulso del deporte inclusivo no atendiendo la partida que reclaban las federaciones. Hay riesgo de desandar el camino
articles.body: En plena semana del deporte inclusivo, una fórmula en la que conviven al mismo tiempo deportistas con y sin discapacidad, chirría que el Gobierno haya congelado en 2026 el dinero destinado al impulso de esta práctica, que quedó reflejado en el Boletín Oficial del Estado el pasado año. En una materia como el deporte, que en esta legislatura se ha incrementado exponencialmente —aunque como pagan tarde, mucho dinero se queda en créditos—, está actitud está en asintonía con un gobierno progresista. La partida de tres millones sigue en los mismos números que en 2025 con el agravante de que se han añadido cinco federaciones y ahora tocan a menos. “Estamos por la labor de impulsar esa política social y nos encanta, pero si no hay ayudas, nos lo vamos a tener que plantear. No somos una federación como la de fútbol que tienen un músculo económico importante”, se quejaba un presidente la semana pasada. El deporte inclusivo, como política de desarrollo de un país, debería estar siempre en las agendas. Para muchos, empezando por este periódico, los éxitos en la competición son casi la razón de ser, pero cualquier político que se precie debe entender que por encima de una canasta, un lanzamiento o una carrera, está que sus ciudadanos compartan la cancha. Las federaciones españolas pidieron aumentar en dos millones de euros la partida. Ynada. Las grandes fuerzas políticas se van a gastar 15 kilos de aquí al 29 de noviembre. Por grosera comparativa. España es un país modélico en ese sentido gracias en gran parte a la aportación privada. Y es uno de esos terrenos en donde a los políticos se les llena la boca de la colaboración público-privada. Quizás no sea necesario que esa cantidad que demandan las federaciones venga del Estado, que tiene otras materias importantes que atender —aunque lo inclusivo es por encima de todo educación y convivencia—, sino incentivos para que muchas empresas desarrollen estrategias en esa dirección. Esté quien esté en 2027 a los mandos de la nave, es un asunto que tiene que mejorar. Porque todo lo que se ha avanzado en combatir la discriminación de género, y la gran metamorfosis también del deporte paralímpico, tiene una grave grieta si esta inclusividad física no se considera como debe.

articles.title: Between parents' struggles and 'endless coffees': How Savitha Shri became India's only gold medallist at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Savitha Shri Baskar emerged as India's golden girl at the 2026 Chess Olympiad, but there was a point when her chess career was funded by her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Savitha Shri Baskar emerged as India's golden girl at the 2026 Chess Olympiad, but there was a point when her chess career was funded by her father's gold jewellery, pawned to cover a national tournament's entry fee.Baskar, an electrician in Singapore at the time, would go on to quit that job entirely and move back to India to support her daughter. It was a decision he still calls difficult.The sacrifice, in fact, wasn't only his to make. Chess had first entered the family through Savitha's older brother Mugesh, whom their father had originally set out to build a career around.Savitha's own interest came from watching him play. But once both children were training together, the costs made running two chess careers impossible. Mugesh stepped back after the eighth standard. Savitha kept going.This time, she went to Samarkand as the youngest member of the Indian contingent, brought in after Harika Dronavalli, who felt she'd achieved everything a chess career could offer, including a gold, stepped aside for the next generation.Even then, there were questions about the 19-year-old International Master's spot in the squad. "There were a lot of people who questioned her spot, journalists saying there are players higher than her, and so on," women's captain Swayams Mishra had earlier told TimesofIndia.com."But according to the selection, she was qualified, and she'd won the Asian continental a couple of months ago. She'd also played the World Women's Team Championship, so I knew her as a team player always. Whenever we gave her the opportunity, she delivered. If India won a medal, we owe it to her."Savitha delivered in some style, becoming the only Indian to win an individual gold medal in Uzbekistan, finishing an extraordinary 9/10, and a central figure in India's bronze-medal campaign.A reserve who ended up playing almost every round"Coming to the team as a reserve player, I wasn't even expecting to play all 10 rounds," she told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "So I'm grateful for the trust my teammates and my captain had in me, for giving me the opportunity to play all 10. I'm happy with the score, 9 out of 10; but game-wise, I think I could have done a bit better."Around her sat some of the biggest names in Indian women's chess. Looking back at her first experience of the Olympiad, she continued, "It was my first Olympiad, and it has always been a dream for me to play for the country in a tournament like this. We had Humpy (Koneru) akka, who's been the top-most player in women's chess for almost two decades, and we had Vaishali akka and Divya Deshmukh; such a strong team, and we were the first seed in the women's section. I learned a lot from all of them, and Abhijit sir and Swayams sir did a wonderful job with our openings and in every other aspect too. It was a wonderful experience."Despite the individual gold, she's unambiguous about where her priorities sat throughout. "The team medal will always come first, because we're giving out everything for the team. I wasn't even caring about my individual gold; someone told me I'd already secured a medal before the last round, but I only found out I'd won gold after the round finished," she recalled with a laugh. "I was just trying my best to win that last game so we could get a silver as a team. From the position I got, I couldn't really convert anything, but I'm at least happy we got the bronze."A murky start, and the climb back from Kazakhstan and ChinaThe campaign didn't begin smoothly off the board. "When we arrived (in Samarkand) at the hotel, it was around 11:30 at night, and they said they couldn't get the rooms ready," Savitha told this website. "We didn't get our rooms for five or six hours. They made us wait in the lobby, then gave one or two rooms for the whole team."What followed, though, was a federation stepping up as Savitha confirmed, "After that, AICF made sure everything was sorted, and that we got our Indian food every day. The Indian restaurant was so far away that they had to arrange someone to get the delivery done, and they made sure the food was good quality and on time. I don't think any federation would have done that. We're all so grateful for it."On the board, the campaign's defining stretch came against Kazakhstan and China, the two matches where her own result decided India's fate."With both teams, I was the one playing till the last point, and my game was going to be the deciding factor," she said. "It started with Kazakhstan; I got an equal position and was trying to push it. I think what helped me score was time management: after move 40 I was always ahead on the clock compared to my opponent, which put more pressure on them, and I was able to swindle the position."Against China, the margins were just as tight. "It's a bit sad we couldn't win that one," the teenager added. "When I got a better position, Vantika made a blunder at that point and got into a worse position. If she'd been able to hold a draw, I think we'd have got gold fairly easily."The captain who brought the 'endless coffees'Through the toughest stretches, Savitha points to one figure in particular for keeping the team together, especially after an early loss to Poland."Swayams sir is the best captain ever, I think, because of the way he handled our team. We lost to Poland, but he was the one who motivated us. Even during games, if we wanted something, he was always there: water, bananas, everything. For me, he was bringing endless coffees, because I played till the last moment every time. He even jokingly said it was because of those coffees that I was able to swing all my games." The backing went beyond logistics, she said. "He had so much confidence in me. I think he believed in me more than I believed in myself."That trust, she added, was something she'd first experienced a cycle earlier, at the Asian Games, and carried with her into Samarkand."There's just so much you learn from being in a team like that, discussing lines together in team meetings, having those interactions, and them having so much confidence in me. They believed in me more than I did in myself at the time too," she noted.Asked whether she thinks back to what her family gave up to get her here, Savitha is candid, albeit guarded, about letting it weigh on her day-to-day. "If I don't play well, it all comes back to mind. My parents struggled. I know what they've gone through, because they had to spend so much on chess because of me. That's something I'll always remember. But I don't really think much about it while I'm playing, or in general. I just have to stay in the present."What's next?Savitha, currently rated 2405, is treating the grandmaster (GM) title as a goal to work toward rather than something owed to her on reputation."The Grandmaster title is definitely my goal, and I'll be working towards it," she said in a confident voice. "I'll be playing tournaments, of course, but for now I think I'll take a bit of rest. The Olympiad is such a big and tiring event. My next tournament will probably be the World Juniors in Namibia, though I might play something before that. I haven't decided yet."On where her game itself needs to sharpen next, she concluded, "In my own game, I think I should get a bit steadier in the openings, and probably work on some positional stuff as well. In the Olympiad, I played the aggressive, complicated positions pretty well; positional chess is the other part I'll be working on."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lionel Messi’s last game for Argentina ends in triumph and tears
articles.summary: Messi scored a goal and created two others as Argentina bid farewell to its most decorated footballer with a 3-0 win.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has delivered ‌one last masterclass in the blue and white of Argentina as its most decorated player and captain, bringing the curtain down ⁠on his extraordinary 21-year ⁠international career by scoring one goal and setting up two others in a 3-0 friendly match against Benin.

The 39-year-old’s final bow came in front of more than 85,000 fans at a packed ⁠Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday. It was less about football and more of a national celebration of Messi’s service to the national team.

Landmarks across the capital glowed with the team’s sky blue and white colours, while fireworks lit up the skies above ⁠the heaving stadium as fans poured their hearts into a rendition of Argentina’s national anthem.

Hours earlier, a huge number 10 shirt emblazoned with “Gracias”, or “Thank You”, was unfurled at the National Flag Memorial in Rosario, Messi’s hometown.

“It’s hard to talk,” said Messi, whose family watched proudly from the stands alongside some of Argentina’s World Cup winners of 1978, 1986 and 2022.

“There are a lot of emotions, a lot of things going through my head. The first thing I think about is ‌my old man,” he added, referring to the recent death of his father.

“It was a huge source of pride for me to wear this shirt all this time, more than 20 years.

“Not coming any more is going to hurt a lot. I swear, I’d love to keep coming my whole life, because playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you.”

As the team bus travelled from the training ⁠centre bearing his name, Messi wiped away tears as thousands lined the route.

When ⁠the teams took the pitch, Benin’s captain looked lost for words as he handed Messi a gift and letter during the pre-match handshake.

After a goalless first half, Messi supplied an assist for Nicolas Otamendi to tap home Argentina’s opener. Otamendi spent 17 years with Messi in ⁠⁠the national team, including four World Cups, and was also ending his international career.

Messi then set up Nico Paz, one of the players seen as a potential successor ⁠for Argentina’s number 10 shirt, to score the second goal.

In a ⁠fairytale ending, Messi converted a penalty for 3-0, his 126th international goal, prompting another round of “Messi, Messi” chants from the crowd.

At the final whistle, teammates, opponents and the referee gathered around Messi for embraces before a drone show lit up the sky. Argentinian singer Soledad Pastorutti, known ‌as “La Sole”, then sang her signature “Brindis” as part of a tribute to Messi and his journey with the national team.

Messi leaves as the country’s most-capped player (208) and record scorer, having transformed years of frustration on the international stage ‌into ‌a story of World Cup and Copa America triumphs.

For years, Argentina asked Messi to deliver. On Tuesday, it simply came to say “Thank You”.

articles.title: España golea a Argentina y llega a las semifinales del Mundial como líder de grupo
articles.standfirst: La selección femenina vence por un contundente 7-1 para seguir invicta en la competición
articles.summary: La selección femenina vence por un contundente 7-1 para seguir invicta en la competición
articles.body: La selección española femenina de hockey patines se clasificó para las semifinales del Mundial que se disputa en Asunción (Paraguay) como primera del grupo A, después de imponerse a Argentina por un contundente 7-1. La victoria ante la selección albiceleste supone un golpe de autoridad de la vigente campeona mundial, que ya había superado a Francia (8-0) y a Chile (2-3), y que afrontará la última jornada de la primera fase ante Suiza, la madrugada de este jueves (1:00 hora española), con el liderato del grupo asegurado y el billete para las semifinales en el bolsillo. Nadie esperaba, sin embargo, un desenlace tan contundente entre las dos selecciones más laureadas de la historia del Mundial. España, con ocho títulos, y Argentina, con seis, se citaban en un duelo que amenazaba con convertirse en la primera gran batalla del campeonato y que, durante los primeros 25 minutos, respondió a ese guion. La igualdad solo se rompió en el marcador a favor de España, que encontró el camino del gol por medio de María Sanjurjo y Aina Florenza para marcharse al descanso con un 2-0 que dejaba todo abierto. Pero el partido cambió radicalmente tras el paso por los vestuarios. Después de sobrevivir 24 horas antes frente a Chile, con el agónico gol de Aina Florenza en el último segundo, España se desató y ofreció una segunda mitad de enorme autoridad. El equipo dirigido por Sergi Macià aceleró, encontró espacios y comenzó a castigar una y otra vez a una Argentina incapaz de contener el vendaval ofensivo español. El 3-1 de Julieta Fernández fue el único momento en el que el conjunto albiceleste logró inquietar a España, pero la reacción fue inmediata. Los goles de Marta Piquero, María Sanjurjo y Aina Florenza terminaron de sentenciar el encuentro y elevaron la diferencia hasta el 6-1, reflejo de la superioridad española en un tramo en el que Argentina se vio completamente desbordada. Victòria Porta puso el broche con el 7-1 definitivo, un resultado que refuerza la candidatura del combinado nacional a revalidar el título. El cuadro argentino, por su parte, deberá jugarse el pase como segunda clasificada en la última jornada ante Chile, en un duelo que decidirá cuál de las dos acompaña a España entre las cuatro mejores del mundo. Goles: 1-0, min.9: María Sanjurjo. 2-0, min.20: Aina Florenza. 3-0, min.29: Marta Piquero, de penalti. 3-1, min.32: Julieta Fernández, falta directa. 4-1, min.32: María Sanjurjo. 5-1, min.42: Aina Florenza. 6-1, min.47: Marta Piquero, de falta directa. 7-1, min.48: Victòria Porta, de penalti. Árbitros: Marco Rondina (ITA) y Luca Molli (ITA). Mostraron tarjeta amarilla al técnico Sergi Macià (min.15) por parte de España y a Luciana Agudo (min.15) por parte de Argentina. Mostraron tarjeta azul a Adriana Soto (min.24) y a Ana Lucía Maldonado (min.40) por parte de Argentina. articles.title: 15 Seconds In, Former Avalanche Defenseman Leaves Game After Big Hit
articles.summary: Former Avalanche defenseman Ryan Lindgren left Tuesday night’s game after taking a hit from behind just 15 seconds into the opening period.
articles.body:
Ryan Lindgren's short stint with the Colorado Avalanche is well in the rearview mirror, but the defenseman made some news Tuesday night.

Lindgren left the Seattle Kraken's game against the Vegas Golden Knights after taking a hit from behind from Vegas forward Marc Gatcomb only 15 seconds into the game.

Lindgren was shaken up on the play but stayed on the bench and continued playing. He did not come back out for the second period, and the Kraken later announced that he would not return because of an upper-body injury.

Nathan MacKinnon following a season-opening win over the Los Angeles Kings.

He finished the game with six shifts and 3:57 of ice time.

The Avalanche acquired Lindgren from the New York Rangers at the 2025 trade deadline. Colorado also received Jimmy Vesey and prospect Hank Kempf, while the Rangers got Calvin de Haan, Juuso Pärssinen and two conditional draft picks.

It was a move that made sense for Colorado at the time. Lindgren was a physical defenseman with plenty of experience, and the Avalanche were looking for help on the blue line. He was also brought in with the possibility of becoming a longer-term replacement for Sam Girard.

Instead, Lindgren spent only a few months in Denver.

He played 18 regular-season games for the Avalanche and had two goals and one assist. He missed the final three games of the regular season before returning for the playoffs.

Colorado used Lindgren against the Dallas Stars in the first round, but the Avalanche were eliminated in seven games.

That ended up being Lindgren's only playoff run with Colorado.

He signed with Seattle during the offseason on a four-year, $18 million contract. The Kraken got 76 games out of him last season, with Lindgren finishing with two goals and seven assists.

He also played in Seattle's first four games this season before Tuesday night.

For the Avalanche, the trade remains a pretty minor footnote in the bigger picture. It also goes down as another Chris MacFarland move that never really came together. Colorado gave up two conditional draft picks and got 18 regular-season games from Lindgren before he left as a free agent.

Lindgren is now in his second season with the Kraken. The next question is how much time he could miss following Tuesday's injury.

articles.title: Rhyne Howard and Dream coach comment on Allisha Gray ahead of New York Liberty
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream are due to return to playoff action on Wednesday evening, aiming to take another step towards this year’s WNBA Finals. After seeing off the...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are due to return to playoff action on Wednesday evening, aiming to take another step towards this year's WNBA Finals.

After seeing off the Washington Mystics in the first round, the Dream secured a 92-82 win over the New York Liberty in the first game of their series over the weekend.

Two more wins will put them into the final against the Golden State Valkyries or the Las Vegas Aces, but it appears as though they will have to make do without Allisha Gray for their game on October 7.

Rhyne Howard says news on Allisha Gray is 'good'

As shared by Meghan L. Hall on X/Twitter, Dream head coach Karl Smesko provided an update on Gray on Tuesday and said: "Allisha Gray is out tomorrow … Day to day after that."

Hall then quoted her original tweet to provide a follow-up, which included Rhyne Howard describing the news on Gray as 'Good news'.

She wrote: "Quick follow up here: The team appeared to be in good spirits and said Gray was as well.

"News on Gray was described as 'good news' by Rhyne Howard. Asked Smesko about who steps up in the lineup. He didn't get into specifics, but mentioned multiple players helping with gap."

Gray secured seven points and one rebound during the Dream's first meeting with the Liberty.

She was also key to the 2-0 series win over the Mystics, including scoring 22 points in game two.

articles.title: “I’m not going to stop” – Kane vows to keep going after reaching 125 England caps
articles.summary: Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps for England on Tuesday, when the Bayern Munich striker started and bagged a brace in a 3-0 win over Cz...
articles.body:
Harry Kane equalled Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps for England on Tuesday, when the Bayern Munich striker started and bagged a brace in a 3-0 win over Czechia.

Speaking in a post-match interview (via ITV), Kane reflected on his future, saying he feels he has plenty more to give at the age of 33.

"125 caps? Beyond my wildest dreams. I hope there's still more to go. I guess only time dictates that. I still feel like I've got room to improve. I've just come back off my best season ever at 32 years old and right now I feel in an even better place," Kane said.

"I'm not going to stop. I'm going to keep pushing and see where it takes me. Maybe in 10 years or so, we'll see where that ceiling is at."

Kane's brace on Tuesday also took him closer to another significant milestone: scoring 100 goals for England. The 33-year-old now has 91 goals for the Three Lions.

Asked if reaching 100 goals for England is his next target, Kane responded:

"It's funny, I've been asked this question from a few of the staff. I think to represent your country that many times is the extreme privilege. The 100 goals is maybe a more exclusive club and being a striker I think could be an incredible club to be a part of.

"I'm getting closer to the 100 now and it's there being in the 90s and I try not to think about it too much and it's like, I guess being a cricketer in the 90s, I think the more you think about 100, it's sometimes harder to achieve. I'm just going with the flow right now. I'm in a fantastic place."

articles.title: How Williams wants to avoid a repeat of its 2026 “disaster” next year
articles.summary: Williams’ campaign has been underwhelming thus far, but James Vowles has cause to believe things will be better in 2027
articles.body:
There are several reasons why Williams ' 2026 "disaster" won't reoccur in the next Formula 1 season, team principal James Vowles believes.

As F1 switched to new technical regulations this year, Williams started the campaign on the back foot. The team missed the Barcelona pre-season 'shakedown', and its FW48 initially was 28kg overweight. It took more than six months to reach the minimum weight, with the introduction of a brand-new chassis at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in late September.

After finishing fifth in last year's constructors' championship, the nine-time world champion outfit is down in ninth this season, with just 12 points to its name.

"I own the mistakes that we made this winter," Vowles said in Malaysia.

When asked by Motorsport.com whether he was confident of avoiding similar pitfalls and if the team was in good shape for 2027, the Briton replied: "I'm confident that we won't have any of the disaster we had this winter.

"In part, we have to accept, though, that's not as big a load that we're putting through the business because the chassis is already here. They're in front of you right now. That does make a considerable difference.

"But what have we done? We've changed actually quite a bit of the software systems, ways of working. We've brought in Piers [Thynne], who has been an absolutely brilliant godsend help in that regard."

Piers Thynne, son of Sheridan (Williams' commercial director in the 1980s and early 1990s), joined Williams in August. He previously spent nearly two decades at McLaren , where he rose through the ranks from a gearbox specialist role to become its chief operating officer in 2023.

"We have information we just simply didn't have one year ago that allows us to make a better call on that," Vowles continued.

"What you're not aware of, and no one here can be, is we think we're doing a good job with development in the wind tunnel and across systems, but you don't know until you turn up at the first race next year."

Back in Baku, Carlos Sainz qualified ninth – Williams' best result of the season – and scored the team's first point since the Monaco Grand Prix.

Asked to assess the upgrade that was introduced in Azerbaijan, Vowles explained there would be much more to come in 2027: "Chassis will carry over into next year. A lot of it was actually forward investing into making sure that's right.

"It's nice to see the car had ballast on it, so directionally correct, but it's too late in the season. That's the facts behind it. We haven't added enough aerodynamic performance. We've focused our cost cap dollars really on just getting the elements right that we need next year, and that was at the sacrifice. We left quite a bit of performance in the tunnel at home."

articles.title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns to India T20I squad after four-year gap
articles.summary: In a significant announcement, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been picked for the Indian T20I squad for the much-anticipated series in New Zealand. With his last inte...
articles.body:
New Delhi: Pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar has made a comeback to the Indian T20I team after four years, having played his last international match in New Zealand in November 2022. The selectors named the 36-year-old while picking a second-string pace attack for the five-match series in New Zealand starting October 22. Bhuvneshwar has led the Royal Challengers Bengaluru pace attack in their two back-to-back IPL-winning campaigns over the last two seasons. The four selectors and Centre of Excellence (CoE) head VVS Laxman met in Guwahati on Tuesday to pick the T20I and India 'A' teams while holding back the ODI and Test teams for the same tour. TOI has learnt that the selectors want to preserve their first-choice pacers for the longer formats with next year's World Cup and the ongoing World Test Championship in mind. The other pacers picked for the T20I series are Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav, with Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube being the seam-bowling allrounders. Ravi Bishnoi has been dropped, while Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakravarthy have been given the spin duties.

Selectors wait for Hardik, Prasidh's fitness status

The selectors are waiting to get clear fitness status on Hardik Pandya and Prasidh Krishna before announcing the ODI and Test teams. Sources said Hardik was ruled out for at least four weeks as per the fitness report shared by the CoE on September 23. Krishna, too, walked off with a hamstring injury during the second ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati on September 30. In a boost to the seam-bowling attack, Akash Deep has been picked for the 'A' team and is expected to be an integral part of the Test team.

Test batters KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant, Dhruv Jurel, Devdutt Padikkal and Washington Sundar have been picked for the India 'A' team, which is scheduled to play three first-class matches before the two Tests starting on November 19. Jurel is named the captain of the team. Pant, who had requested game time in New Zealand, has been picked subject to fitness after he suffered a back spasm during the Irani Cup last week. He is also recovering from a viral illness and could take another 10 days before he starts training. Interestingly, ODI regulars Rahul, Jaiswal and Washington may have to juggle formats as the 'A' series overlaps with the ODI series, which starts on November 4. That means the trio may play the first 'A' game on October 24 before joining the ODI team.

India's T20I squad: Shreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wk), Tilak Varma (vc), Axar Patel, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Prince Yadav, Mayank Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Kuldeep Yadav.

articles.title: What Happened To Enzo Amore's Proposed WWE Return (WWE News)
articles.summary: Enzo Amore was reportedly in talks to return to WWE earlier this year.
articles.body:
With various reports earlier this year that Enzo Amore and Big Cass were set to make a return to WWE , only one half of that story has played out.

Of course, Big Cass returned in August, and he's spent the past couple of months targeting the likes of Je'Von Evans, Dragon Lee, and Rey Mysterio on the Raw brand.

Speaking on Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer said that there was indeed a plan for both Cass and Enzo Amore to return to WWE, but that plan called for the two to be kept separate. Instead of reuniting the classic Enzo and Cass pairing, Enzo would have been used in NXT, with WWE not wanting to limit Cass' upside by having him in a tag team.

Meltzer was told that Enzo's return was "pretty much a done deal", though it appears those talks didn't get over the line, as Smacktalker Skywalker has yet to turn up in NXT, or on any other WWE brands, for that matter.

For those who may have missed the initial reports, it was back in May that word first came out that WWE was looking to bring back Enzo and Big Cass , at a time when Big Bill 's AEW contract was expiring imminently . It was then reported that Amore had been spotted at the WWE Performance Center, adding further fuel to these rumblings. Vignettes would start airing on Raw hyping up Cass's return for August 3rd , with many presuming that Enzo would be alongside his seven-foot-tall pal. However, Cass has been used as a singles act since returning.

articles.title: Tom Pidcock furious after two teammates hit by police motorbike during race in Italy
articles.summary: The issue is the latest in a string of incidents involving vehicles on race courses
articles.body:
Tom Pidcock said a police motorbike driving the wrong way during a race in Italy crashed into two of his teammates, with one of them requiring stitches as a result.

The Pinarello Q36.5 leader ultimately finished second at Tre Valli Varesine, a one-day race in Lombardy, behind Lotto-Intermarche's Jarno Widar, but his challenge by hampered by two of his key lieutenants crashing.

Spaniard Marcel Camprubi and Briton Thomas Gloag were knocked off their bikes by the errant police vehicle with six laps of the finishing circuit remaining. Camprubi was able to continue but Gloag abandoned the race.

Pidcock told race broadcaster Eurosport: "A police motorbike was going the wrong way down the course and crashed into two of our guys. So from this point... well, first of all I wanted to stop racing myself. I was mad. The guys all riding in front of me, for me, and two of them on the floor.

"Luckily Marcel was okay, he could continue. Tom [Gloag] was also okay, in the end, but he stopped the race, and he has some stitches in the knee.

"Things like this shouldn't happen. But we continued and got back into the race and I'm happy that I could be on the podium."

The incident is the latest in a spate of issues concerning rider safety and course security, which has put scrutiny on race organisers' ability to properly secure routes.

The issue has dominated headlines since Welsh rider Finlay Tarling was killed at the Volta a Portugal race in August after a vehicle outside the race convoy entered the course and collided with him at high speed.

Pidcock dedicated his victory at the mountain bike world championships later that month to the 19-year-old , while the riders' union, the Cyclistes Professionnels Associes (CPA), has led calls for enhanced safety at races.

Six riders have been killed during road races in the last three years, while several races have seen incidents involving errant public vehicles getting onto the course, with rider Maeve Plouffe nearly hit by a motorist during the women's Tour of Britain this summer.
